title: "Show me the market"
hook: offered half his brother's wealth, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf asks only to be shown the market (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the people of the bench, poor companions living in the mosque. Your line was: the bench of the poor.

Two strangers, made brothers. When the emigrants arrived in Medina with almost nothing, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, paired them up with the people of the city. Newcomers were given local brothers. Bukhari keeps one of those pairings in the newcomer's own words. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from Mecca, is paired with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', from Medina. And Sa'd, almost at once, makes him an enormous offer. Today: show me the market.
screen: `STRANGERS MADE BROTHERS.` → `ABD AL-RAHMAN AND SA'D.` → `AN OFFER ON THE TABLE.`

segments.voice: Sa'd says, in Abd al-Rahman's telling: I am the wealthiest of the Ansar. I will divide my wealth in half, and half is yours. Weigh that. Not a meal or a loan: half of everything, to a man he has just met, because the Prophet called them brothers. Abd al-Rahman answers, in effect: I have no need of that. Is there a market here where trade goes on? Sa'd tells him: the market of Qaynuqa. The next morning Abd al-Rahman is there. He buys and sells dried curd and clarified butter, small goods, and keeps going back, day after day. Before long, Bukhari says, he turns up with a trace of yellow perfume on him, the sign of a bridegroom. He has earned enough to marry. Neither man is the hero alone. Sa'd's generosity is real and total: he offered half, and meant it. Abd al-Rahman's refusal isn't pride. He answers with thanks, and with a blessing on Sa'd's family and wealth. What he asks for instead is a door: not the money, but the place where money is honestly made. Both are kindness. One gives. The other protects the giver, and keeps his own dignity. The brotherhood stayed whole.
screen: `HALF OF EVERYTHING IS YOURS.` · `IS THERE A MARKET HERE?` · `CURD AND BUTTER, DAY AFTER DAY.` · `ONE GIVES, ONE PROTECTS THE GIVER.` · then, large: `SHOW ME THE MARKET.`

segments.voice: Think about your work, paid or unpaid, and the way you earn what you have, and let yourself be glad of one place where it's honest and clean. Then notice one place that could be cleaner, a shortcut, an exaggeration, a corner cut, and simply see it, without arguing with it. If you pray, you can ask Allah to bless what you earn.
Qaynuqa, the market Sa'd sent him to, where Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf earned his own way instead of taking half his new brother's wealth. Today's word.
Your line: a trace of yellow perfume. He asked for the door, and walked through it himself. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims tell the story of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' when speaking of the brotherhood (mu'akhah) between the emigrants and the Ansar, and of earning an honest living.

what a scholar hears: Bukhari 2048 and 2049, Abd al-Rahman's own report; the brotherhood (mu'akhah) and the market of Banu Qaynuqa.

chat.says: Why didn't Abd al-Rahman just accept half of Sa'd's wealth?
options: He blessed Sa'd and asked for the market instead, to earn his own way.
He was too proud to accept help from anyone in Medina.
He didn't trust that Sa'd really meant the offer he made.
chat.meaning: He thanked and blessed Sa'd, then asked: is there a market here? Both were kind: one gave, the other protected the giver.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.meaning: an emigrant from Mecca who asked for the market

Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'.meaning: his brother in Medina, who offered half his wealth

Ansar.meaning: the helpers: the believers of Medina

Qaynuqa.meaning: the market Sa'd sent him to

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2048 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: brotherhood with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'; offer of half his wealth; the market of Qaynuqa; dried curd and butter; the trace of saffron)

notes: Bukhari 2048 and 2049 numbers cited from memory; confirm.
In the hadith Sa'd also offers to divorce one of his two wives so that Abd al-Rahman could marry her; left out of the script for this audience. Confirm the omission is acceptable.
'I am the wealthiest of the Ansar' is Sa'd's own claim in the hadith, reported as his words; confirm.
Abd al-Rahman's blessing on Sa'd's family and wealth is in Bukhari 2049 (Anas); confirm.
'Paired them up with the people of the city': the mu'akhah; script gives no count of pairs.

Editor pass: cut the flourish 'by a single word' from the hook (no cited text says how the pairing was made); 'Think about what that offer means' became 'Weigh that offer' to avoid the banned 'Think' opener pattern.
